narrative:
On November 19, 2026, the Karnataka High Court achieved an overall hearing clearance rate of 45.0%, taking up 1,285 of the 2,853 scheduled matters across 53 judges. This represents a significant rebound from the preceding day's 23.3% clearance rate (655 heard of 2,810 scheduled on November 18), closely aligning with earlier performance benchmarks such as 44.0% on November 13 and 36.0% on November 12.

Procedural stage efficiency drove much of the volume. Matters listed for Orders constituted the largest share of the docket, converting at 52.9% (514 of 972 heard), a sharp rise from the 28.4% recorded on November 18. Admission matters reached 43.8% (285 of 650), while Preliminary Hearings saw 41.8% taken up (183 of 438). Notably, Final Hearings improved to 22.5% (104 of 462), recovering markedly from the 4.0% clearance observed during the previous session.

In terms of subject matter, Writ Petitions dominated the causelist with 1,132 listings, registering 519 hearings (45.8%)—more than double the prior day's 21.8% rate. Miscellaneous First Appeals and Criminal Petitions maintained steady momentum, converting at 45.7% (211 of 462) and 46.7% (190 of 407), respectively. Higher clearance rates occurred in Civil Revision Petitions (76.3%), whereas Income Tax Appeals lagged considerably at 10.0% (4 of 40) and Regular First Appeals converted at 23.4% (40 of 171).

Bench-level outputs varied substantially across court halls. High-volume clearance was led by Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty, who heard 122 matters across two rosters (60 of 95 in Hall 20 and 62 of 92 in Hall 21), and Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar, who took up 98 cases across Hall 22 lists. In contrast, several extensive lists experienced heavy bottlenecks; the division bench in Hall 5 heard none of its 58 scheduled cases, and Hall 31 cleared only 3 of 109 cases (2.8%) on its primary cause list.
